extracted.intended_audience: regulated employers, industry stakeholders, economists, and public commenters on OSHA's heat rule (NPRM)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting the economic-impact cost categories and breakdowns from the OSHA heat NPRM tables (cost estimates by industry and region for specific compliance actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Costs for Humidity Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Total estimated costs for implementing humidity control, reported by region (Alaskan, Central, Eastern, Pacific, Southern, Western) and by industry sector (listed sectors and subtotals), with an overall Total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table presents numeric cost estimates (broken out by region and sector). This chunk contains raw numeric values without narrative explanation; use accompanying NPRM text for assumptions and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Employee Acclimatization—Designated Person
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs associated with assigning a designated person for acclimatizing new employees, reported by industry sector and region with subtotals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a table of numeric costs by sector and region. No procedural guidance in this chunk on how designation is defined or implemented; refer to NPRM text for operational definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Employee Acclimatization—Designated Person
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for assigning a designated person to acclimatize returning employees, broken down by industry and region, with subtotals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table-only presentation in this chunk; the metric captures costs specific to acclimatization of returning employees via a designated person.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Indoor Employee Acclimatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for acclimatizing new employees who work indoors, reported by industry sector and region and aggregated to subtotals and totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric table; distinction between indoor/outdoor acclimatization is a key dimension of the analysis (see separate indoor/outdoor entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: New Outdoor Employee Acclimatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for acclimatizing new employees who work outdoors, reported by sector and region with subtotals and totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a separate table to reflect differing costs/assumptions for outdoor work compared with indoor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Indoor Employee Acclimatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for acclimatizing returning indoor employees, with a region-by-sector breakdown and aggregated totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide numeric cost estimates; the returning-employee category is treated separately from new employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning Outdoor Employee Acclimatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for acclimatizing returning outdoor employees, broken down by industry sector and region with subtotal and total rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate accounting for outdoor returning-employee acclimatization costs; numeric values only in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rest Breaks at Initial Heat Trigger—Indoor
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for providing rest breaks when the initial heat-trigger threshold is reached for indoor workers, reported by industry sector and region (rows show numeric estimates and subtotals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table appears to show multiple numeric subcolumns (e.g., possibly total, first-year, annualized) but the chunk contains only raw numbers; consult the NPRM's table header/footnotes for exact column meanings and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Costs for Rest Breaks at Initial Heat Trigger—Indoor
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate total costs for indoor rest breaks triggered by the initial heat threshold, summed across regions and sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the aggregated impact for the specific compliance action (rest breaks at the initial trigger) as presented in the NPRM tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Sector Breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs and estimates are reported across a set list of industry sectors used as evaluation dimensions: Agriculture, Forestry, and Fishing; Building Materials and Equipment Suppliers; Commercial Kitchens; Construction; Drycleaning and Commercial Laundries; Landscaping and Facilities Support; Maintenance and Repair; Manufacturing; Oil and Gas; Postal and Delivery Services; Recreation and Amusement; Sanitation and Waste Removal; Telecommunications; Temporary Help Services; Transportation; Utilities; Warehousing; Non-Core; and Totals/subtotals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector-level disaggregation is a primary organizing principle of the economic tables; analyses and comments should consider sector heterogeneity and consult sector definitions in the NPRM preamble or economic appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost estimates are broken down by geographic regions: Alaskan, Central, Eastern, Pacific, Southern, and Western; subtotals and totals aggregate across these regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional disaggregation allows assessment of geographic variation in costs. The chunk lists region names and numeric values but not the regional definitions—refer to NPRM methodology for region definitions and weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtotal / Total Aggregation Rows
rubrics_metrics.description: Each table includes subtotal rows for groups of sectors and overall total rows that aggregate costs across sectors and regions (e.g., Subtotal, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to how subtotals are constructed (which sectors are included in ‘Non-Core’ vs core categories) and whether totals represent sums of present-value or annualized amounts—full table headers/notes in the NPRM are required to interpret correctly.
